name: Tuber melanosporum

size_cm.source: CNR-IBBR 2025, TuberID database, record 9: Tuber melanosporum Vittad.
size_cm.note: ascocarp 3 to 5 cm, up to 10 cm; globose or irregular

notes: Short-distance type, as most ectomycorrhizal ascomycetes are [12]; native to EU, in orchards elsewhere. Tuber species in culture grow only 0.6 to 0.9 mm in 40 days, a genus figure not entered as a tip speed, and a 2025 model study links warm dry summers to soil mycelium growth [24]. Reported (unchecked) to kill surrounding plants in a "burnt" circle, to need two mating types and to have a sequenced genome.

tip_speed.note: Iotti M, Amicucci A, Stocchi V, Zambonelli A 2002, Morphological and molecular characterization of mycelia of some Tuber species in pure culture, New Phytologist 155:499-505 (https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1469-8137.2002.00486.x). The abstract, which was read, gives 1.1 to 14 mm/week across six Tuber species; a search snippet of the full text gives 1.1 to 1.9 mm/week for T. melanosporum in the exponential phase (full text not opened). Midpoint 1.5 mm/week = 0.21 mm/day = 8.9 um/h. Medium and temperature not seen

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

t_opt.note: Colony growth on YpSs agar at 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 33 C was best at 20 and 25 C and worst at 33 C (Liou C-F 2010, doctoral thesis, National Taiwan University, abstract only, https://tdr.lib.ntu.edu.tw/handle/123456789/46767). 22.5 C is the midpoint of the two best temperatures; no colony sizes are given in the abstract

t_min.note: Group figure, not this species alone: T. aestivum, T. borchii, T. melanosporum and T. rufum are said to grow between 5 and 34 C with the optimum between 15 and 26 C, in the introduction of Nakano et al. 2022, Mycoscience 63(2):53-57 (https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/mycosci/63/2/63_MYC564/_html/-char/ja), citing older work that was not opened

t_max.note: Group figure, not this species alone; see t_min (Nakano et al. 2022, Mycoscience 63(2):53-57, https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/mycosci/63/2/63_MYC564/_html/-char/ja). Consistent with 33 C being the worst temperature in Liou 2010
